My guess is that unless the US economy totally cratered, it is unlikely there would be a sudden and severe movement away from the dollar as a reserve currency. And the effects on the US economy would be felt in a moderate increase in the cost of imports (itself in part fueled by a lessening of the export of finance). But it isn't as though the euro or yen or yuan or ruble or pound or peso would suddenly replace the dollar.
